notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended February 28, 2025, as the village reported them in its F-65 Annual Local Unit Fiscal Report to the Michigan Department of Treasury. Not a budget.
Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included. Residents also pay Lapeer County and the township the village is part of.

Spending is reported by function for the general fund, other governmental funds, enterprise funds (water, sewer and other utilities) and component units (such as downtown development authorities). Internal service funds ($107,359 of their revenue and spending) are left out, since the departments they serve report that spending.
Borrowing, transfers between funds, sales of capital assets, depreciation and extraordinary items are left out.
General government, courts, community and economic development, and redevelopment and public housing count as overhead.
Debt is total long-term debt at year end, as reported on the F-65.
Political money is not scored: Michigan local candidates file campaign finance reports with their county clerk, not with the state.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.
